newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African jailed 40 years for murdering two Britons.
newsitem.headline: S.African jailed 40 years for murdering two Britons.

text.p: A 26-year-old man who hacked two British tourists to death in an "unbelievably savage attack" in South Africa four years ago was on Wednesday sentenced to 40 years in jail.
Passing sentence on Elias Sibiya, Justice Piet Combrinck said he had never dealt with such a brutal killing.
"This was an unbelievably savage attack and it is incomprehensible how one human being can do this to other human beings," Combrinck said in the Mtunzini Magistrates' Court in KwaZulu-Natal province.
"In my 30 years in the legal profession I have never seen such terrible wounds. I can only describe it as butchering, a frenzy of violence."

With a machete and spear Sibiya hacked and stabbed Julie Godwin and Elizabeth Over on the remote northern KwaZulu-Natal coast at Sodwana, stole their jewellery and money, and dumped their bodies in the sea.
Sibiya handed himself over to the police exactly four years after the November 1992 murders. At his first court appearance he said he killed on an order from God.
But in his latest testimony Sibiya said he murdered the women out of his hatred for white people because they forcibly removed his parents from their home during the apartheid era.

"It is unfortunate that you said that you killed them out of hatred for white people because they mistreated blacks in the past. I could find no evidence in your earlier statements to corroborate this. Therefore...I have to make the inference that you acted out of greed."
Combrinck said the stiff sentence was meant to deter other criminals and to put a brake on the spiral of violence and murder in South Africa.
